newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury to issue first indexed note on Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury to issue first indexed note on Jan 15.

text.p: The Treasury Department will issue its first inflation-indexed security, a 10-year note, on Jan 15 and expects to add another maturity within a year, senior department officials said Wednesday.

The exact auction date for the January sale was not specified, but Treasury said that after the first auction they will be sold on a quarterly basis and issued on the 15th of January, April, July and October.
Treasury is assessing demand for the new security that protects investors against the ravages of inflation, but said the first auction will be "in the billions" of dollars' worth.

The seminannual interest payments on inflation-protected securities will be taxed as current income. In addition, any increase in the inflation-indexed principal must be reported as interest income in the year in which it occurs so that taxes can be charged.

In a separate release, the White House said that by January 1998 there also will be available inflation-protected U.S. savings bonds in amounts as small as $50. Earnings on them will be tax-deferred until they are cashed in and they will be available through payroll savings plans as well as from Treasury and banks.
Traditional savings bonds, known as EE bonds, will continue to be sold along with the inflation-protected variety.
